title: Image Classification Quiz
description: Test your understanding of image classification

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of extracting features from images before classification?
options: To make images look better
To reduce dimensionality while preserving important information
To increase the number of pixels
To convert images to grayscale
questions.explanation: Feature extraction reduces the high dimensionality of raw pixel data while preserving the most important information for classification. This makes processing more efficient and can improve model performance.

questions.question: What activation function is used in the hidden layer of our image classifier?
options: Sigmoid
Tanh
ReLU (Rectified Linear Unit)
Softmax
questions.explanation: ReLU (Rectified Linear Unit) is used in the hidden layer. It outputs max(0, x), introducing non-linearity while being computationally efficient and helping to avoid vanishing gradient problems.

questions.question: Why do we use softmax activation in the output layer for multi-class classification?
options: It makes training faster
It converts outputs to probabilities that sum to 1
It reduces the number of parameters
It prevents overfitting
questions.explanation: Softmax converts the output layer's raw scores (logits) into probabilities that sum to 1. This allows us to interpret the outputs as confidence levels for each class and makes the model's predictions probabilistic.

questions.question: What does the cross-entropy loss function measure?
options: The distance between predicted and actual pixel values
The difference between predicted probabilities and true class labels
The number of misclassified images
The complexity of the neural network
questions.explanation: Cross-entropy loss measures how different the predicted probability distribution is from the true distribution (one-hot encoded labels). Lower loss means better predictions, with perfect predictions having zero loss.

questions.question: What is the purpose of L2 regularization in image classification?
options: To speed up training
To increase model accuracy on training data
To prevent overfitting by penalizing large weights
To reduce the number of classes
questions.explanation: L2 regularization adds a penalty term proportional to the square of the weights. This discourages the model from relying too heavily on any single feature and helps prevent overfitting, leading to better generalization on unseen data.

questions.question: In a confusion matrix for a 3-class problem, what does the diagonal represent?
options: Misclassified samples
Correctly classified samples
Total number of samples per class
Prediction confidence scores
questions.explanation: The diagonal of a confusion matrix shows correctly classified samples - where the predicted class matches the true class. Off-diagonal elements represent misclassifications between different classes.

questions.question: What happens if the learning rate is set too high?
options: Training becomes very slow
The model always achieves perfect accuracy
Training may become unstable and loss may oscillate or diverge
The model will underfit the data
questions.explanation: A learning rate that's too high causes large weight updates, which can make training unstable. The loss may oscillate wildly or even increase (diverge) instead of decreasing smoothly toward a minimum.

questions.question: What is the role of the hidden layer in a neural network?
options: To store the training data
To learn intermediate representations and feature combinations
To display the final predictions
To normalize the input features
questions.explanation: The hidden layer learns intermediate representations by combining input features in non-linear ways. This allows the network to detect complex patterns and relationships that aren't directly visible in the raw features.

questions.question: How does increasing the hidden layer size affect the model?
options: It always improves accuracy
It increases model capacity but may lead to overfitting
It reduces training time
It has no effect on performance
questions.explanation: Increasing hidden layer size gives the model more capacity to learn complex patterns. However, too many neurons can lead to overfitting, where the model memorizes training data instead of learning generalizable patterns.

questions.question: What is the main limitation of using a simple feedforward neural network for image classification compared to CNNs?
options: It cannot handle color images
It requires manual feature extraction and doesn't preserve spatial relationships
It can only classify two classes
It trains much slower than CNNs
questions.explanation: Simple feedforward networks require pre-extracted features and treat them as independent values, losing spatial relationships. CNNs automatically learn hierarchical features directly from pixels while preserving spatial structure through convolution operations.
